## Proof

**Setup.** Let $S^{2}=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{3}:x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=1\}$ carry the symplectic form $\omega$ equal to the standard area form, obtained by contracting the Euclidean volume form with the outward unit normal $N=x\,\partial_{x}+y\,\partial_{y}+z\,\partial_{z}$:

$$\omega \;=\; \iota_{N}(dx\wedge dy\wedge dz)\Big|_{S^{2}} \;=\; \bigl(x\,dy\wedge dz \;-\; y\,dx\wedge dz \;+\; z\,dx\wedge dy\bigr)\Big|_{S^{2}}.$$

The Hamiltonian is $H(x,y,z)=z$, so $dH = dz$.

**Claim.** The Hamiltonian vector field $X_{H}$, defined by $\iota_{X_{H}}\omega = dH$, is

$$X_{H} \;=\; -y\,\partial_{x} \;+\; x\,\partial_{y},$$

i.e. the infinitesimal generator of rotation about the $z$-axis.

**Verification.** First, $X_{H}$ is tangent to $S^{2}$, since
$$\langle N, X_{H}\rangle \;=\; x(-y)+y(x)+z(0) \;=\; 0.$$

Compute $\iota_{X_{H}}\omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ (with $a=-y,\;b=x,\;c=0$):
$$\iota_{X_{H}}\omega \;=\; x\bigl(b\,dz-c\,dy\bigr) \;-\; y\bigl(a\,dz-c\,dx\bigr) \;+\; z\bigl(a\,dy-b\,dx\bigr)$$
$$= x^{2}\,dz \;+\; y^{2}\,dz \;-\; zy\,dy \;-\; zx\,dx \;=\; (x^{2}+y^{2})\,dz \;-\; zy\,dy \;-\; zx\,dx.$$

Using $x^{2}+y^{2}=1-z^{2}$ on $S^{2}$:
$$\iota_{X_{H}}\omega \;=\; (1-z^{2})\,dz \;-\; zy\,dy \;-\; zx\,dx \;=\; dz \;-\; z\bigl(z\,dz+y\,dy+x\,dx\bigr).$$

Restricting to tangent vectors of $S^{2}$, differentiating $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=1$ gives $x\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz=0$, so the parenthesized term vanishes on $TS^{2}$. Hence

$$\iota_{X_{H}}\omega\Big|_{S^{2}} \;=\; dz \;=\; dH,$$

confirming $X_{H}=-y\,\partial_{x}+x\,\partial_{y}$.

**Integrating the flow.** The ODE $\dot\gamma = X_{H}(\gamma)$ reads
$$\dot x = -y,\qquad \dot y = x,\qquad \dot z = 0.$$

Thus $z$ is conserved (consistent with $H=z$ being conserved along its own flow), and $(x,y)$ undergoes uniform rotation:
$$x(t)=x_{0}\cos t - y_{0}\sin t,\qquad y(t)=x_{0}\sin t + y_{0}\cos t,\qquad z(t)=z_{0}.$$

**Conclusion.** The Hamiltonian flow of $H=z$ on $(S^{2},\omega)$ is rotation about the $z$-axis with unit angular velocity:

$$\boxed{\;\varphi_{t}(x,y,z) \;=\; \bigl(x\cos t - y\sin t,\;\; x\sin t + y\cos t,\;\; z\bigr).\;}$$

Geometrically this is expected: $H=z$ is the height function, its level sets are latitudes, and the Hamiltonian flow preserves $H$ while moving each latitude circle at constant speed — precisely a rigid rotation about the polar ($z$) axis. The period is $2\pi$, and the flow is periodic with all orbits closed (circles of latitude, degenerating to fixed points at the poles $(0,0,\pm1)$, which are exactly the critical points of $H$).
